description: An open-source bastion host (jump server) for SSH, RDP, VNC and Telnet with web access, session recording, audit logs and Casdoor SSO

latest_release.name: v2.0.0
latest_release.body:
## Changelog
### Features
* 9cee10808eaac677b30807981b092224564406d4 feat: add system accounts with password rotation, and access requests that administrators approve
* 380805e5bb91d23ab0057c1a7368c22ddc10dcc0 feat: connect to MySQL and PostgreSQL assets in the browser and audit the SQL
* 8fc8a993fa042ca90555109fa8fdf7bd37a27d7b feat: copy images and files between the browser and RDP sessions through the clipboard
* 9b9395f6f1bba51a930706dbbd5cf21233dc2b33 feat: export audit logs as CSV and forward them to syslog
* 0846eaa801d77ba1bddb3555e6d6e2eab769593a feat: forward local ports to RDP, VNC and other assets through the SSH gateway
* 5acab8848a4e4d5422eded74d9d9f59ab2565dd0 feat: put an image copied on this machine on the RDP clipboard when the page gets the focus
* e32ce38a5e75c3dfb09a715e05a734c1edad6e14 feat: run commands, scripts and file transfers on many SSH assets at once
* 033f120b6994726feb5f76324a9a6a09438b0147 feat: serve the Go profiles on a local address when pprofAddr is set
* 500a3f839d187a60ec8e3b9abaa3c88dd6481ba1 feat: sign in to local accounts with a code from an authenticator app
### Bug fixes
* c8c795aaedff2310f212ffe086bf486488240a9d fix: close the RDP viewer when the session ends and reconnect after a dropped connection
* 56c19a475eeb3e70076e09fa9ceb77321e45c176 fix: hold the VNC clipboard and gateway commands to the clipboard and file permissions
* 593fbffae0231de9d43a8795866187331dfa7431 fix: keep Chrome from freezing background connection pages, which closes their WebSockets
* 6ed7c4c9f2db77cf5a66320a30b7ebd17df483c5 fix: keep retrying with a growing delay when reconnecting to an RDP session fails
* 6dc603047979daa88905e5c22afd22de8c8b1b76 fix: let approvals only narrow access requests and check database exports against the session's account
* a4cc1b332d116f8f10591f6f2e7d6220851dd465 fix: release keys the RDP screen lost the release of, so Ctrl does not stay down
* 3a4f889cce680eb311f2bd17230c7c8d52ee8964 fix: reload connection pages left open across a server upgrade

detail.readme:
📦⚡️ Casvisor

An open-source bastion host (jump server) for SSH, RDP, VNC and Telnet, written in Go and React.

Online demo | Documentation | Issues | LINUX DO

Casvisor sits between the people who run your servers and the servers themselves. People open SSH, RDP, VNC and Telnet sessions from a browser tab, or use their own `ssh`, `scp` and VS Code through Casvisor's SSH gateway. They only reach the servers a permission gives them, never see the servers' passwords, and every session is recorded. - **One Go binary.** All four protocols are handled inside Casvisor, with nothing to install on the servers. It runs on SQLite with its own accounts out of the box. - **Apache-2.0, no enterprise edition.** Recording, the SSH gateway, network gateways and everything else in this README are in the open-source project. - **Policy you can read.** Permissions are enforced with [Casbin](https://casbin.apache.org), and sign-in can be handed to [Casdoor](https://casdoor.ai) for SSO, MFA, LDAP and social logins. ## Features **Connect** - **SSH** in an xterm.js terminal, with a file panel beside it for upload and download over SFTP. - **RDP** with [gordp](https://github.com/casvisor/gordp), a pure-Go RDP client: NLA, the GFX graphics pipeline (ClearCodec, RemoteFX Progressive) like the Windows client, sharp text on high-DPI screens, the remote cursor, clipboard, resizing with the window, and file transfer through a redirected drive. Works with Windows Server, Windows 10/11 and FreeRDP-based hosts such as Ubuntu. - **VNC** with noVNC. Casvisor does the VNC authentication itself, so the password stays on the server. - **Telnet** for network gear and old systems, logging in with the asset's account. - **MySQL and PostgreSQL** in a browser SQL console: the databases, tables and columns on the left, a statement run from the editor or from a selection, one tab per result. Every statement passes the command rules and lands in the command records, and a result can be copied or exported as CSV. Database assets work through network gateways and with system accounts too. - **SSH gateway** on port 2222: `ssh -p 2222 web-01@casvisor.example.com`, `scp`, `sftp`, `rsync`, Xshell and VS Code Remote, signed in with the user's public key and under the same permissions as the browser. - **Port forwarding to any asset** for clients of its own protocol: `ssh -p 2222 -N -L 13389:win-01:3389 alice@casvisor.example.com`, then mstsc, a VNC viewer or a database client connects to `localhost:13389`. Needs the `Forward` action; the bytes pass through as they are, so the user logs in to the asset with its account, and the connection is listed as a session and logged but not recorded. - **Network gateways** for assets Casvisor cannot reach directly: through an SSH jump host, or through an agent that connects out from a private network over HTTPS. - **Stored credentials.** Passwords and private keys are encrypted in the database and filled in by Casvisor. SSH host keys and RDP certificates are pinned on first use. **Control** - **Permissions** on users, groups, assets and asset tags, with the actions `Connect`, `Copy`, `Paste`, `Upload`, `Download` and `Forward`, client IP ranges and a time window. - **System accounts.** An asset can carry several accounts besides its own, such as `root`, `deploy` and `readonly`; permissions decide which account a user may connect with, and the password never reaches the browser. Passwords can be changed by hand or on a schedule, and an account missing on the server can be created and set from Casvisor. - **Access requests.** Users ask for an asset with a reason and an end time, an administrator approves and Casvisor creates the permission; withdrawing it removes the permission and disconnects open sessions. - **Two-step verification** for local accounts, with any TOTP authenticator app. - **Command rules** that block or flag commands matching a regular expression, in the web terminal, the SQL console and through the SSH gateway alike. - **Revocation takes effect at once.** Open sessions are disconnected as soon as their permission or account is edited, deleted or expires. **Audit** - **Session recording and playback** for SSH, Telnet, VNC and RDP, replayed in the browser with the same code that drew them live. SSH and Telnet recordings can be downloaded as asciicast. - **Live monitoring** of online sessions, and stopping any of them. - **Command records** of SSH and Telnet sessions, read off a virtual screen, so tab completion, history and line edits are captured as they ran. - **Operation log** of file transfers and every change made through the API. - **Export and syslog.** Session, command and operation logs export to CSV, and can be forwarded to a syslog server as RFC 5424 JSON or CEF. **Operate** - **Jobs** on many SSH assets at once: a command, a Bash or PowerShell script, or a file to copy, with concurrency, timeouts and per-asset output and exit codes. Command rules apply, and each asset's run is a session. - **Patch management** for SSH assets: scan for pending system updates, install them and restart, on Windows (Windows Update) and on Linux (apt, dnf, yum). - **Web console** in 9 languages, built with React, Vite and shadcn/ui, with a RESTful API and [Swagger docs](swagger). ## Quick start ```shell docker run -d --name casvisor -p 19000:19000 -p 2222:2222 \n -v casvisor-db:/db -v casvisor-recordings:/recordings casbin/casvisor docker logs casvisor ``` Open http://localhost:19000 and sign in as `admin` with the password printed in the log, then change it in **My Account**. Pass `-e adminPassword=` to choose the first password instead. Then add a server under **Assets** and click **Connect**. Administrators reach every asset; to let other people in, add them under **Users** and give them a **Permission**. The repository's [docker-compose.yml](docker-compose.yml) does the same with Docker Compose. Port 2222 is the SSH gateway. Users add their public key under **SSH keys** and connect with `ssh -p 2222 @`. To use mstsc, a VNC viewer or another client of the asset's own protocol, forward a local port with `ssh -p 2222 -N -L :: @`; the asset list copies this command for each RDP, VNC and Telnet asset. ## Installation from source Requires Go 1.23 and Node.js 20 with Yarn. ```shell git clone https://github.com/casvisor/casvisor cd casvisor/web && yarn install && yarn build && cd .. go run main.go ``` Settings are read from [conf/app.conf](conf/app.conf). Put the settings of your own server in `conf/app.local.conf` (same format, not tracked by git), or pass any of them as environment variables. ### Database The default is SQLite: ```ini driverName = sqlite dataSourceName = db/casvisor.db ``` To use MySQL instead (the database is created if it does not exist): ```ini driverName = mysql dataSourceName = root:123456@tcp(localhost:3306)/ dbName = casvisor ``` ### Sign in with Casdoor Instead of its own accounts, Casvisor can sign users in with [Casdoor](https://casdoor.ai), for SSO, MFA, LDAP and third-party logins, and use Casdoor's groups in permissions. Create an organization and an application for Casvisor in Casdoor, add `http:///callback` to the redirect URLs of the application, and set: ```ini casdoorEndpoint = https:// clientId = clientSecret = casdoorOrganization = casdoorApplication = ``` When `casdoorEndpoint` is empty, Casvisor uses its own accounts. ### Recordings Sessions are recorded to `recordings/` under the working directory (`/recordings` in Docker). `recordingPath` moves them, `recordingRetentionDays` deletes the ones older than that many days, and `disableRecording = true` turns recording off. ## Network gateways Assets in another data center, or behind NAT in an office, are reached through a network gateway. Add one under **Network gateways** and pick it in the asset's **Network gateway** field. Every connection to the asset (web SSH, Telnet, VNC, RDP, the SSH gateway and patch management) then goes through it. - **SSH jump host**: a server in that network that Casvisor can log in to over SSH. Nothing is installed on it; its sshd needs `AllowTcpForwarding yes`. - **Agent**: for networks Casvisor cannot connect into at all. Generate a token on the gateway's page and run the agent on any machine in that network: ```shell casvisor agent --server https://casvisor.example.com --token cva_... --fingerprint SHA256:... ``` The agent is the same `casvisor` binary (with Docker: `docker run -d --restart unless-stopped casbin/casvisor agent --server ...`). It connects out to Casvisor's web address over WebSocket, so it works wherever HTTPS gets out, listens on no port, and only connects to the **Allowed networks** set on the gateway. The command shown when generating the token has every flag filled in. See the [documentation](https://casvisor.org) for the token options, host key pinning and how the agent reports its status. ## Architecture | Part | Description | Stack | Source | |----------|-------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------|------------------------| | Frontend | Web console, workbench and session player | TypeScript, React, Vite, shadcn/ui | [web](web) | | Backend | RESTful API, protocol tunnels, SSH gateway | Go, Beego, xorm, SQLite / MySQL | [casvisor](.) | | RDP | Pure-Go RDP client | Go | [casvisor/gordp](https://github.com/casvisor/gordp) | ## Contribute Questions and ideas are welcome in [issues](https://github.com/casvisor/casvisor/issues). Pull requests are welcome too, though we recommend opening an issue first to discuss larger changes. ## License [Apache-2.0](LICENSE)
